chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ibn Baqqah, from Abu Abdillah al-Mumin, from Ammar ibn Abu Aasim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four whose supplication is not answered.' So he mentioned the fourth: a man who had wealth, so he lent it out without a proof. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would say: 'Did I not command you with witnesses?'

key_terms.أَدَانَهُ: He lent it / He made a debt

ai.seo_question: Why is a person's supplication not accepted if they lend money without witnesses?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the acceptance of supplication to adherence to prophetic legal formalities, specifically identifying the failure to secure witnesses in debt as a spiritual impediment. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that ritual piety is incomplete without the meticulous observance of social and financial contracts (bay') prescribed by the Ahl al-Bayt. The divine address underscores that neglecting the evidentiary requirements of wealth management constitutes a direct disobedience to Allah's command, thereby blocking the flow of divine response to one's du'a.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Asimy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Ibn Baqqah, from Abu Abdullah Al Momin, from Ammar Bin Abu Aasim who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There are four who would not be Answered for them (their supplication)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned the fourth one as being a man who had some wealth for him, so he lent it out without a proof. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be Saying: “Did I<sup>azwj</sup> not Command you with the witnesses?”’
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Tamimiy from ibn Baqqah from abu ‘Abd Allah al- Mu’min from ‘Ammar ibn abu ‘Asem who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The prayers of four kinds of people are not heard and accepted and he (the Imam) said that the fourth one is he who has an asset which he lends it to someone without the presence of witness and testimony; and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, then says, “Did I not command you to secure witness and testimony.’””
